# spiDE {.unnumbered .unlisted}

<p class="tagline">Neighbourhood-dependent differential expression for spatial transcriptomics, with patients as the replicates, in R and Python.</p>

::: {.cta}
[Get started](get-started.Rmd){.primary}
[R reference](reference/r/index.html)
[Python reference](reference/python/index.html)
[GitHub](https://github.com/BhuvaLab/spiDE)
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.intro}
spiDE finds neighbourhood-dependent differential expression in spatial transcriptomics. Within an *index* cell type, it asks whether a gene's expression changes with the local density (the *niche*) of another cell type, within patients, and whether that dependence differs between two conditions. Patients are the unit of replication throughout: a triplet's evidence (gene, index type, niche type) is how its niche slope varies between patients, never the number of cells.

This website covers both packages: the R package **spiDE** (Bioconductor) and the Python package **spidepy** (on `AnnData`). They share the method and the documentation, and [R vs Python](r-vs-python.qmd) lists how they correspond.
:::

## Install {.section-title}

::: {.card-sn .install-card}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```r
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")

# development version from GitHub (needs SpaNorm >= 1.7.15)
BiocManager::install("BhuvaLab/spiDE")
```

```r
library(spiDE)
data(toySpiDE)

res <- spiDE(toySpiDE, condition = "condition", sigma = 30)
results(res, test = "pooled")      # niche-dependent expression, across patients
results(res, test = "condition")   # its difference between the conditions
```

## Python

spidepy is not on PyPI yet. The extra index gives a CPU-only build of PyTorch, which it needs through spanormpy:

```bash
pip install --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu "spidepy @ git+https://github.com/BhuvaLab/spidepy.git"
```

```python
import spidepy as sp

adata = sp.datasets.toy_spide()
res = sp.spide(adata, condition="condition", sigma=30)
sp.results(res, test="pooled")      # niche-dependent expression, across patients
sp.results(res, test="condition")   # its difference between the conditions
```

:::

:::

## How it works {.section-title}

Function names are given for R; spidepy uses the same steps as `build_niches()`, `fit_spide()` and `test_spide()`.

1. **Niches** (`buildNiches()`): per sample, a Gaussian kernel density of every cell type at every cell.
2. **Fit** (`fitSpiDE()`): for every index cell type, one negative binomial GLM per gene on the niche densities with an intercept per patient, fitted with [SpaNorm](https://github.com/BhuvaLab/SpaNorm)'s Newton solver. Each niche coefficient is a within-patient slope.
3. **Test** (`testSpiDE()`): the **pooled** test (is the slope non-zero, consistently across patients?) always, and the **condition-specific** test (does it differ between conditions?) when given a condition.

### Authors

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
# Authors card, generated from Authors@R in ../DESCRIPTION. The role line is built from the
# MARC codes; only the maintainer (cre) gets a mailto: link.
ppl <- eval(parse(text = read.dcf("../DESCRIPTION", fields = "Authors@R")[1, 1]))
role_name <- c(aut = "author", cre = "maintainer", fnd = "funder", ctb = "contributor",
               ths = "thesis advisor", cph = "copyright holder")
for (p in ppl) {
  r <- p$role
  lab <- if (all(c("aut", "cre") %in% r)) "author and maintainer" else
    paste(unname(role_name[r]), collapse = ", ")
  nm <- paste(p$given, p$family)
  if ("cre" %in% r && length(p$email))
    lab <- sprintf("%s ([%s](mailto:%s))", lab, p$email, p$email)
  orcid <- p$comment[["ORCID"]]
  icon <- if (!is.null(orcid) && nzchar(orcid))
    sprintf(" [![ORCID](https://orcid.org/assets/vectors/orcid.logo.icon.svg){.orcid fig-alt=\"ORCID\"}](https://orcid.org/%s)", orcid) else ""
  cat(sprintf("- %s, %s%s\n", nm, lab, icon))
}
```
